title: Frontend: Topological Sort (BFS)
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Topological Sort (BFS). This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({count,edges}) using Kahn indegree removal. Always choose the smallest ready vertex. Return the deterministic order; throw Cycle if not all vertices can be emitted.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Compute each vertex’s indegree, enqueue all zero-indegree vertices, and remove them one by one while decrementing outgoing neighbors.
alternativeApproaches: Produce dependency layers for concurrent execution while preserving a separate cycle-reporting path.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Independent nodes; diamond; cycle.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
